open_points.subject: one-home rollout invariant
open_points.text: “no other service keeps a customer record or a copy of its values” conflicts with “Production Registry starts without waiting for the other services” and the acknowledged copies that remain until each service changes
open_points.question: Is the one-home rule an invariant required when production starts, or a migration target under which named temporary copies may remain?
options: Require every service and legacy instance to remove its copies before production starts
Allow a transition period and enumerate the permitted temporary copies and their removal condition
open_points.default_guess: Treat it as a migration target and allow only the temporary copies explicitly recorded by governance.

open_points.subject: object characteristics under the one-home rule
open_points.text: The trust boundary classifies “the object's address and identifying characteristics” as `personal_data`, while R0-80's one-home rule names only “the object's address” among object values held only by Registry
open_points.question: Are identifying characteristics also forbidden from being kept by other services, or does the one-home restriction apply only to the address?
options: Apply the one-home rule to both address and identifying characteristics
Apply it to the address only while allowing services to retain characteristics
open_points.default_guess: Apply the one-home rule to every object field classified as `personal_data`, including identifying characteristics.

open_points.subject: meaning of a kept copy
open_points.text: “read them by `customer_ref` or project id when they use them” and “read when it is used, not kept” do not say when transient use becomes a prohibited copy
open_points.question: Which forms and lifetimes of storage count as keeping a copy—process memory, request caches, queues, retries, logs, backups, or persisted database fields?
options: Forbid persistence beyond the request or operation that uses the value
Permit bounded caches with a declared lifetime
Forbid only authoritative customer records while permitting ordinary service snapshots
open_points.default_guess: Allow the value only for the duration of the operation that needs it and forbid persistence in caches, queues, logs, databases and backups unless an explicit exception applies.

open_points.subject: issued-document exception
open_points.text: “except as fixed in a document it issued” and “A document a service issues” do not define when a draft or generated artifact becomes an issued document
open_points.question: What observable event makes a document eligible to retain fixed personal values, and can drafts, regenerated versions or unsent estimates use the exception?
options: Only an immutable document finalized and sent or formally posted is issued
Any generated document artifact is issued
Each document-owning service defines issuance independently
open_points.default_guess: Treat only a finalized immutable document that has been sent or formally published as issued; drafts do not qualify.

open_points.subject: Client Portal offline projection contents
open_points.text: The projection may hold “only what the customer's own cabinet shows, never a tax id,” but the same text says “contact data still reaches the owner alone”
open_points.question: May Client Portal's offline projection contain the customer's name or other contact data, or must those values be excluded despite being visible in the customer's cabinet?
options: Exclude all customer contact data and tax data
Allow selected contact fields shown to that customer
Allow every cabinet-visible field except tax id
open_points.default_guess: Exclude contact data and tax data; permit only project identity and publication values explicitly needed by the customer-facing cabinet.

open_points.subject: customer erasure and fiscal data
open_points.text: “erase a customer's contact data” removes only “name, phone, e-mail and language,” while R0-67 says this is “the end of its record” leaving only identity and the erased fact, and R0-80 adds tax id and legal name to the Customer
open_points.question: Does customer erasure also remove tax id, legal name, kind, restriction state and relationship-ended state, or do any of them survive?
options: Remove every customer value except `customer_ref` and the erased marker
Remove contact fields but retain fiscal and lifecycle fields
Provide separate contact-data and full-personal-data erasures
open_points.default_guess: Remove every customer value except `customer_ref` and the erased marker, matching R0-67.

open_points.subject: missing billing data
open_points.text: Fiscal data is accepted only “when given,” but “read a customer's billing data” promises tax id, legal name and, for a person, the full name without defining the result when those values were never recorded
open_points.question: What does the billing-data operation do when a required document value is absent?
options: Refuse with a missing-billing-data failure identifying absent fields
Return nullable or omitted fields
Derive missing legal or full names from the customer name
open_points.default_guess: Refuse with a specific missing-billing-data failure and identify the absent required fields without returning partial billing data.

open_points.subject: audit coverage of new state changes
open_points.text: Registry logs “only significant changes of state,” illustrated by a non-exhaustive-looking list, while the new actions also register sessions, replace and answer requests, change active projects, publish or withdraw pointers, add rooms, archive projects and import data
open_points.question: Exactly which accepted and refused actions create audit entries?
options: Audit every durable mutation and its outcome
Audit only the mutations expressly enumerated in R0-58
Declare a precise per-action audit flag
open_points.default_guess: Declare audit behavior per action and audit every durable security-, identity-, access-, erasure- and publication-related mutation, but not ordinary reads.

open_points.subject: revision guard for owner changes
open_points.text: R0-29 says “Every change ... made against an older revision is refused,” but R0-35 defines revisions only for projects and customers, while owner changes also affect session access, pending requests, import state and the audit log
open_points.question: Which revision or concurrency token must accompany each owner mutation outside Project and Customer, and what is the failure when it is stale?
options: Use the session access version for every session mutation and define equivalent versions for import and audit state
Limit stale-revision checks to Project and Customer changes
Give every mutable aggregate its own revision
open_points.default_guess: Give each mutable aggregate a concurrency version, using the existing access version for session access, and require it on every owner mutation of that aggregate.
